notes: Test prompts for the skill. Assertions are deliberately not written yet — they get drafted while the first run is in flight. Read references/schemas.md for the full shape.

evals.name: auth-surface-audit
evals.prompt: can you do a UI pass on our signup + login pages? i want to know if anything looks off, especially on mobile. app is running on localhost:8080
evals.expected_output: Runs probe-stack, scaffolds a write zone, defines flows for the auth surface including deliberate error states, smoke-tests, captures, produces evidence-backed findings with severity and evidence paths, and reports synthetic-data caveats if the backend is unreachable.
assertions: Runs scripts/probe-stack.mjs before dispatching any worker
Reports the API ladder verdict (real / bypass / emulated) explicitly
Includes an error state in the flow spec, not just the empty form
Every finding carries an evidence path that exists on disk
Every finding carries either a measurement or a sourceHint
States plainly if backend data is synthetic
Does not modify any file outside the git-ignored write zone
Final answer includes a count of findings by severity and the coverage totals

evals.name: multi-flow-sweep-with-priorities
evals.prompt: I want a full visual regression across the main app before we ship v2 — maybe 8 or 10 of the main journeys. what should we actually fix first?
evals.expected_output: Fans out one worker per flow, then clusters findings into root causes and leads with the tier-1 items where one change clears many findings, rather than listing findings in severity order.
assertions: Fans out per flow rather than auditing everything in one context
Runs a smoke test before fanning out
Clusters findings into root causes with counts
Leads the report with a small number of one-line fixes that clear the most findings
Names a source file or line for at least the top causes

evals.name: false-p0-trap
evals.prompt: run the visual audit on the library / decks area. i expect there's a broken route in there somewhere
evals.expected_output: Discovers the route fails because a declared dependency is absent from node_modules, and reports it as an environment limitation rather than a product P0.
assertions: Checks whether the cause is a declared-but-uninstalled dependency before calling it a defect
Does not file the environment fault as P0 or P1
Records the fault in a limitations section, not the severity table
States the exact command to fix it and re-run
